title: Buffer Solutions and Titrations - Chemistry - Titration Curves
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which titration curve features an equivalence point at exactly pH 7.00 (at 25°C)?
options: Weak Acid titrated with Strong Base
Strong Acid titrated with Weak Base
Strong Acid titrated with Strong Base
Weak Acid titrated with Weak Base
questions.explain: The titration of a strong acid with a strong base produces a neutral salt and water. At the equivalence point, the pH is determined solely by the autoionization of water, which is pH 7.00 at 25°C.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: During the titration of a **weak acid** with a **strong base**, the pH at the equivalence point is:
options: Depending solely on the indicator used
questions.explain: At the equivalence point of a weak acid/strong base titration, all the weak acid ($$ \text{HA} $$) has been converted to its conjugate base ($$ \text{A}^- $$). The conjugate base undergoes hydrolysis ($$ \text{A}^- + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HA} + \text{OH}^- $$), producing hydroxide ions and resulting in a basic solution (pH > 7).
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: On the titration curve of a weak acid with a strong base, at which point is the pH equal to the $$ \text{p}K_a $$ of the weak acid?
options: At the start of the titration
questions.explain: At the half-equivalence point, exactly half of the weak acid has been neutralized, meaning $$ [\text{HA}] = [\text{A}^-] $$. Using the Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a + \log(1) $$, so $$ \text{pH} = \text{p}K_a $$.
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is it difficult to obtain a precise end point when titrating a weak acid with a weak base?
options: The indicator reacts with the weak base.
There is no steep vertical section in the titration curve near the equivalence point.
The reaction is too fast to monitor.
The pH remains constant throughout the titration.
questions.explain: In a weak acid/weak base titration, the pH change near the equivalence point is very gradual (no sharp inflection point). This lack of a steep vertical section makes it difficult for any indicator to show a sharp color change at the specific equivalence volume.
